paragraphs: As used in this report, the terms "we," "us," "our," "GEO" and the "Company" refer to The GEO Group, Inc., its consolidated subsidiaries and its unconsolidated affiliates, unless otherwise expressly stated or the context otherwise requires.

We specialize in the ownership, leasing and management of secure facilities, processing centers and reentry facilities and the provision of community-based services in the United States, Australia and South Africa. We own, lease and operate a broad range of secure facilities including maximum, medium and minimum-security facilities, processing centers, as well as community-based reentry facilities. We develop new facilities based on contract awards, using our project development expertise and experience to design, construct and finance what we believe are state-of-the-art facilities. We provide innovative technologies, industry-leading monitoring services, and evidence-based supervision and treatment programs for community-based programs. We also provide secure transportation services domestically and in the United Kingdom through our joint venture GEOAmey Ltd. ("GEOAmey"). As of December 31, 2025, our worldwide operations include the management and/or ownership of approximately 75,000 beds at 95 secure and community-based facilities, including idle facilities, and also includes the provision of reentry and electronic monitoring and supervision services for thousands of individuals, including an array of technology products including radio frequency, GPS, and alcohol monitoring devices.
We provide a diversified scope of services on behalf of our government agency partners:
• our secure facility management services involve the provision of security, administrative, rehabilitation, education, and food services at secure services facilities;

• our reentry services involve supervision of individuals in community-based programs and reentry centers and the provision of temporary housing, programming, employment assistance and other services with the intention of the successful reintegration of residents into the community;
• we provide comprehensive electronic monitoring and supervision services;
• we develop new facilities, using our project development experience to design, construct and finance what we believe are state-of-the-art facilities;
• we provide secure transportation services; and
• our services are provided at facilities which we either own, lease or are owned by our government agency partners.

We conduct our business through four reportable business segments: our U.S. Secure Services segment; our Electronic Monitoring and Supervision Services segment; our Reentry Services segment and our International Services segment. We have identified these four reportable segments to reflect our current view that we operate four distinct business lines, each of which constitutes a material part of our overall business.

Our U.S. Secure Services segment primarily encompasses our U.S.-based public-private partnership secure services business. Our Electronic Monitoring and Supervision Services segment, which conducts its services in the U.S., consists of our electronic monitoring and supervision services. Our Reentry Services segment consists of various community-based and reentry services. Our International Services segment primarily consists of our public-private partnership secure services operations in Australia and South Africa. Financial information about these segments for years 2025, 2024 and 2023 is contained in Note 14 — Business Segments and Geographic Information included in the notes to our audited consolidated financial statements included in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.
On February 6, 2026, J. David Donahue, our Chief Executive Officer, provided notice to us of his retirement effective February 28, 2026 (the "Separation Date").

Mr. Donahue and GEO entered into a Separation Agreement and General Release on February 9, 2026 (the "Separation Agreement"). Pursuant to the terms of the Separation Agreement, Mr. Donahue will be entitled to receive the following in addition to accrued wages: (i) the payment of $104,167 per month commencing on March 1, 2026 and continuing through February 28, 2028 in accordance with the terms of the Consultant Agreement described below; (ii) be entitled to the payment of health insurance premiums for himself and any covered dependents under the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act ("COBRA") for a period ending on the earlier of eighteen (18) months following the Separation Date (or up to twenty-four months if entitled to an extension) or the date he is no longer entitled to receive COBRA continuation coverage; and (iii) the outstanding unvested stock options and restricted stock previously granted to Mr. Donahue will continue to vest in accordance with the applicable performance-based vesting metrics under our long-term equity incentive plan. The Separation Agreement also contains mutual release, cooperation and non-disparagement provisions.

Mr. Donahue and GEO also entered into a Consultant Agreement (the "Consultant Agreement"), effective as of March 1, 2026, for a term continuing through February 28, 2028 (the "Consulting Period"). Pursuant to the terms of the Consultant Agreement, Mr. Donahue will provide consulting services to GEO with respect to secure services business opportunities in the United States and overseas, including business development services and contract administration assistance for existing contracts. In consideration for such services, Mr. Donahue will receive, as previously disclosed in the Separation Agreement, the consulting fee of $104,167 per month during the Consulting Period, payable upon submission of a monthly billing statement, and will be reimbursed for reasonable and necessary documented travel and business expenses incurred in connection with the performance of services, subject to prior approval requirements. The Consultant Agreement also contains provisions related to confidentiality and conflicts of interest.

Our level of indebtedness could adversely affect our financial condition and prevent us from fulfilling our debt service obligations.
We are incurring significant indebtedness in connection with substantial ongoing capital expenditures. Capital expenditures for existing and future projects may materially strain our liquidity.
Despite current indebtedness levels, we may still incur more indebtedness, which could further exacerbate the risks described above.
Because portions of our senior indebtedness have floating interest rates, an increase in interest rates would adversely affect cash flows.
We depend on distributions from our subsidiaries to make payments on our indebtedness. These distributions may not be made.
We may not be able to satisfy our repurchase obligations in the event of a change of control or fundamental change because the terms of our indebtedness or lack of funds may prevent us from doing so.
The value of the collateral may not be sufficient to satisfy our obligations under the Secured Notes.
Efforts to reduce the U.S. federal deficit could adversely affect our liquidity, results of operations and financial condition.
paragraphs: The risk factors summarized and detailed below could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, or results of operations, impair our future prospects and/or cause the price of our common stock to decline. Additional risks not currently known to us or those we currently deem to be immaterial may also materially and adversely affect our business operations. Material risks that may affect our business, operating results and financial condition include, but are not necessarily limited to, those relating to:
• Public and political opposition to the use of public-private partnerships could have a material adverse effect on our business.
• Our level of indebtedness could adversely affect our financial condition and prevent us from fulfilling our debt service obligations.
• We are incurring significant indebtedness in connection with substantial ongoing capital expenditures.
• We may still incur more indebtedness which could further exacerbate the risks we face.
• The covenants in the indentures governing our outstanding Secured and Unsecured Notes and our Credit Agreement impose significant operating and financial restrictions.

This section of this Form 10-K generally discusses 2025 and 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussions of 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this Form 10-K can be found in "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in Part II, Item 7 of the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 and are incorporated herein by reference.

We specialize in the ownership, leasing and management of secure, reentry facilities and processing centers and the provision of community-based services in the United States, Australia and South Africa. We own, lease and operate a broad range of secure facilities including maximum, medium and minimum-security facilities, processing centers, and community-based reentry facilities. We offer counseling, education and/or treatment for alcohol and drug abuse problems at most of the domestic facilities we manage. We are also a provider of innovative compliance technologies, industry-leading monitoring services, and evidence-based supervision and treatment programs for community-based parolees, probationers and pretrial defendants. Additionally, we have a contract with ICE to provide supervision and reporting services designed to improve the participation of non-detained aliens in the immigration court system. We develop new facilities based on contract awards, using our project development expertise and experience to design, construct and finance what we believe are state-of-the-art facilities that maximize security and efficiency. We also provide secure transportation services for offender and detainee populations as contracted domestically and in the United Kingdom through our joint venture GEOAmey.

As of December 31, 2025, our worldwide operations included the management and/or ownership of approximately 75,000 beds at 95 correctional, detention and reentry facilities, including idle facilities, and also included the provision of servicing individuals in a community-based environment on behalf of federal, state and local correctional agencies located throughout the country.

For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we had consolidated revenues of $2.6 billion and $2.4 billion, respectively and we maintained an average company-wide facility occupancy rate of 89.2% including 68,157 active beds and excluding 6,646 idle beds for the year ended December 31, 2025, and 87.2% including 67,604 active beds and excluding 11,675 idle beds for the year ended December 31, 2024.

The consolidated financial statements in this report are prepared in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles, or GAAP. As such, we are required to make certain estimates, judgments, and assumptions that we believe are reasonable based upon the information available. These estimates and assumptions affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements and the reported amounts of revenue and expenses during the reporting period. A summary of our significant accounting policies is described in Note 1 – Summary of Business Organization, Operations and Significant Accounting Policies of the notes to the audited consolidated financial statements contained in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. paragraphs: 如本報告所用，"we"、"us"、"our"、"GEO"及"the Company"均指The GEO Group, Inc.及其合併子公司與未合併附屬公司，除非另有明確說明或語境另有要求。

我們專門從事美國、澳洲及南非的政府機構夥伴之安全設施、處理中心及再入獄設施的所有權、租賃及管理，以及社區服務之提供。我們擁有、租賃並營運廣泛的安全設施，包括最高、中度及最低安全級別設施、處理中心，以及社區型再入獄設施。我們根據契約獎勵開發新設施，運用我們的專案開發專業知識與經驗，設計、建造並融資我們認為為最先進的設施。我們提供創新科技、業界領先的監測服務，以及基於證據的監督與治療方案，用於社區型計畫。我們亦透過我們的合資公司GEOAmey Ltd.（"GEOAmey"）提供國內及英國的安全運輸服務。截至2025年12月31日，我們的全球營運包括管理及/或擁有約75,000個牀位的95個安全及社區型設施，包括閒置設施，並包含為數千名個人提供再入獄及電子監測與監督服務，包括一系列科技產品，如無線電頻率、GPS及酒精監測裝置。
我們代表政府機構夥伴提供多元化服務範疇：
• 我們的安全設施管理服務涉及在安全服務設施提供安全、行政、復健、教育及餐飲服務；
• 我們的再入獄服務涉及監督社區型計畫及再入獄中心的個人，並提供臨時住宿、計畫、就業協助及其他服務，以期居民成功重新融入社區；
• 我們提供全面的電子監測與監督服務；
• 我們開發新設施，運用我們的專案開發經驗設計、建造並融資我們認為為最先進的設施；
• 我們提供安全運輸服務；
• 我們的服務由我們擁有、租賃或由我們政府機構夥伴擁有之設施提供。
我們透過四個應報告分部進行業務：我們的美國安全服務分部；我們的電子監控與監督服務分部；我們的重返服務分部以及我們的國際服務分部。我們已識別這四個應報告分部，以反映我們目前的觀點，即我們經營四個不同的業務線，每一個皆為我們整體業務的重要組成部分。

我們的美國安全服務分部主要涵蓋我們美國基地的公私合作安全服務業務。我們的電子監控與監督服務分部，其服務業務於美國進行，包含我們的電子監控與監督服務。我們的重返服務分部包含各種社區基於及重返服務。我們的國際服務分部主要包含我們在澳洲及南非的公私合作安全服務業務。關於這四個分部於2025年、2024年及2023年的財務資訊，請參閱第14節 — 商業分部及地理資訊，包含於我們經審計合併財務報表的附註中，並包含於本年度報告表10-K第二部分，第8項。
2026年2月6日，我們的首席執行官J. David Donahue通知我們，他將於2026年2月28日（稱為「離職日期」）退休。

Donahue先生與GEO於2026年2月9日簽訂離職協議與一般釋放書（稱為「離職協議」）。根據離職協議的條款，Donahue先生除已積累的薪資外，將有權獲得以下補償：(i) 自2026年3月1日起，每月支付104,167美元，持續至2028年2月28日，根據下述諮詢協議的條款；(ii) 有權獲得根據《綜合預算協調法案》（「COBRA」）為自己及其任何受保依賴人支付健康保險 premiums，持續至離職日期後十八（18）個月（或最多二十四個月，若符合延長條件）或他不再有資格獲得COBRA延續保障之日；以及(iii) Donahue先生先前授予的未實現股票選擇權及限制性股票將根據我們長期股權激勵計劃的適用績效基準認購條件繼續認購。離職協議亦包含雙方釋放、合作及不貶低的條款。

Donahue先生與GEO亦於2026年3月1日簽訂諮詢協議（稱為「諮詢協議」），有效期至2028年2月28日（稱為「諮詢期間」）。根據諮詢協議的條款，Donahue先生將為GEO提供諮詢服務，關於美國及海外的安全服務業務機會，包括業務發展服務及現有合同的合同管理協助。作為對此服務的報酬，Donahue先生將根據離職協議先前披露的內容，在諮詢期間每月獲得104,167美元的諮詢費用，於每月提交發票後支付，並可獲得與執行服務相關的合理且必要的旅行及業務費用的補償，但須經事先批准。諮詢協議亦包含有關保密及利益衝突的條款。

本 Form 10-K 的此部分一般討論 2025 年與 2024 年的項目及 2025 年與 2024 年的年對年比較。未包含於本 Form 10-K 的 2023 年項目及 2024 年與 2023 年的年對年比較，可於本公司 2024 年 12 月 31 日財務年度的年度報告 Form 10-K 中「管理階層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」部分找到，並 hereby 並入參考。

我們專門從事美國、澳洲與南非的 Secure, Reentry 設施與處理中心的所有權、租賃與管理，以及社區服務的提供。我們擁有、租賃並營運廣泛的 Secure 設施，包括 Maximum, Medium 與 Minimum-Security 設施、處理中心與社區型 Reentry 設施。我們在大多數國內設施中提供諮商、教育與/或治療服務，以處理酒精與藥物濫用問題。我們也是創新合規科技、行業領先的監測服務與基於證據的監督與治療方案的提供者，服務社區型假釋人、緩刑人與預審被告。此外，我們與 ICE 簽有契約，提供監督與報告服務，以提高非拘留外國人參與移民法庭系統的參與度。我們根據契約獎勵開發新設施，運用我們的專案開發專業與經驗，設計、建造與融資我們認為為最先進的設施，以最大化安全與效率。我們也透過與 GEOAmey 的合資公司，為違法者與拘留者羣體提供安全運輸服務，服務範圍包括美國與英國。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的全球營運包括管理與/或擁有約 75,000 張牀位的 95 處矯正、拘留與 Reentry 設施，包括閒置設施，並包括為美國各地聯邦、州與地方矯正機構的個體提供社區型服務。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日，我們的合併營業收入分別為 2.6 十億美元與 2.4 十億美元，我們維持平均公司整體設施使用率為 89.2%，包括 68,157 張活躍牀位，排除 6,646 張閒置牀位；以及 87.2%，包括 67,604 張活躍牀位，排除 11,675 張閒置牀位。

本公司負債水平可能不利於財務狀況，並可能妨礙本公司履行債務償還義務。
本公司因重大持續資本支出而產生顯著負債。現有及未來專案的資本支出可能嚴重影響本公司流動性。
儘管目前負債水準較高，我們仍可能增加更多負債，這可能會進一步加劇上述風險。
由於我們部分高階負債具有浮動利率，利率上升將會不利於現金流。
我們依賴子公司提供的資金來償還負債，這些資金可能無法兌現。
在發生控制權變更或根本性變更的情況下，我們可能無法履行回購義務，因為負債條款或資金不足可能阻止我們這麼做。

努力減少美國聯邦政府財赤可能會不利於我們的流動性、營運成果與財務狀況。
paragraphs: 風險因素彙總並詳細說明於下，可能會重大且不利地影響我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果，影響我們未來的發展前景，並/或導致我們普通股的價格下跌。尚有其他未被我們所知或目前認為不重要之風險，也可能重大且不利地影響我們的業務營運。可能影響我們業務、營運成果與財務狀況的重大風險包括，但不僅限於：
• 公眾與政治對公私合作模式之反對，可能會對我們的業務造成重大且不利的影響。
• 我們的負債水平可能會不利地影響我們的財務狀況，並使我們無法履行債務償還義務。
• 我們因重大持續資本支出而產生顯著負債。
• 我們仍可能產生更多負債，這可能會進一步加劇我們所面臨的風險。
• 我們現有 secured and unsecured notes 以及 credit agreement 所規範之契約條款，會對我們的營運與財務狀況施加重大限制。
